ledger.claim: The three artifacts that carry this dispute describe one trip and nothing about the measurement is in doubt: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown each carry trip_id TRP-02839, and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-21T18:23:08+08:00 matches the trip_record started_at to the second. The rider has discharged POL-RD-08(a).

The trace measures the driven distance at 24.6 km against a booked optimal of 20.0 km, an excess of 4.6 km and 23.0% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates are passed (more than 0.8 km absolute and more than 20% of optimal), and POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km — not the rounded trip_record copy — the governing field. The deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own evidence.

Nothing here needs corroboration from outside the trace: 193 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds mean the trace satisfies none of POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c), so the deviation may be established on the trace alone and no independent source is required.

ledger.claim: The driver's 'KPE closed, LTA advisory on file' answer is an exoneration only if POL-RD-03 limb (c) is met, that is, an actual route that leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after. The trace does not show it: 0 fixes fall inside the advisory's area and the vehicle's closest approach to it is 1350.67 m, and the optimal route's own polyline is absent from the record. A limb that cannot be verified on the admitted evidence does not discharge the driver's burden under POL-RD-08, and an unverified limb exonerates nothing.

If the closure does not exonerate, the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary, and it runs on the booked optimal route under POL-RD-02: charged_total is $35.01; the recomputed fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 20.0 + 0.28 x 27.0) x the 1.0 surge multiplier read from fare_breakdown) + $0.80 platform fee + $0.00 ERP on the optimal route = $27.16; the refund is therefore $35.01 - $27.16 = $7.85. That is above the $0.50 de minimis floor and is only 22.4% of charged_total, far short of the 90% at which a full refund would issue, so the rider asks for PARTIAL_REFUND of the $7.00 he contested.

The $3.00 ECP Fort Rd eastbound line is a crossing the booked route never makes: fare_breakdown records on_optimal_route false for that gantry and optimal_route_erp_sgd of 0.00, so the optimal-route recomputation carries no ERP at all. The trace's nearest fix to the gantry is 59.1 m at 18:39:08, so under POL-RD-09's 250 m match rule the crossing is real and the line is not a phantom charge — but it is a gantry the rider did not ask to cross. If the closure exoneration is found instead of a deviation, POL-RD-09(2) still refunds that off-route ERP to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at $12.00, because the rider did not cause the closure either; and since the justified excess (4.6 km) equals the measured excess (4.6 km), no excess remains to be refunded under POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal route.

On the primary route the $3.00 is inside the $7.85 and must not be added to it: POL-RD-09(1) provides that where a deviation is refunded under POL-RD-02, off-route ERP is already comprehended in that refund, because the recomputed fare carries only on-optimal-route gantries and here carries $0.00 of ERP. The rider claims the comprehended figure, not a doubled one.

The measured excess on the governing trace figure is 4.60 km and 23.00%, and the platform's own closure arithmetic justifies the whole of it: the POL-RD-03 cap is min(measured 4.60 km, 1.30 x (23.0 - 20.0) + 1.00 = 4.90 km), so no part of the excess falls outside the cap and nothing remains to be refunded under POL-RD-02. The closure-adjusted optimal distance is 24.6 km, which is exactly the distance the driver drove and exactly the distance billed.

The advisory the driver relies on is on file and satisfies POL-RD-03(a) and (b). EV-ADVIS-02839-01 is a HIGH-severity CLOSURE on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway towards ECP after Defu Flyover, active 2026-08-21 17:53:08 to 19:20:08, which wholly covers the trace window of 18:23:08 to 18:55:08; the platform records intersects_route true and overlaps_trip_window true for it, and the record gives a shortest lawful alternative of 23.0 km against a booked optimal of 20.0 km.

The route driven is the diversion, not a deviation. The driver's trace records zero fixes inside the advisory's area and a closest approach of 1350.67 m to it, so the vehicle never traversed the closed segment at all - which is the substance of limb (c), that the actual route leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after. Because the optimal route's own polyline is not carried in the record, this is the closest test of limb (c) the record permits, and it points the driver's way.

The driver's traffic excuse is not the weightless assertion POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13 discard. It names a specific artifact, EV-ADVIS-02839-01, and a specific clause, POL-RD-03, and that advisory covers the trip window. This is the converse of the case POL-RD-13 addresses - there the bundle holds no advisory and the assertion carries no weight; here the advisory is present, admissible at full weight, and discharges the burden POL-RD-08 shifts onto the driver.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern and therefore no basis for any uplift or referral. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 197, a ratio of about 0.005, which is below both the 3-flag count and the 0.05 ratio POL-RD-06 requires. POL-RD-06(b) therefore cannot upgrade any refund to FULL_REFUND of the charged total, and POL-RD-06(c) cannot refer the driver to conduct review. No other profile field may be used for this test, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

The deviation is not material on any view. The excess is 23.00% against the 50% material threshold and 4.60 km against the 8.0 km material threshold, and materiality is assessed on the excess remaining after the POL-RD-03 adjustment, which is nil. The POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is therefore not even engaged, let alone satisfied.

Because the deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-09(2) leaves the distance and time charges standing - the driver is not at fault for the KPE closure, and the rider did not cause it either. The distance and time component of the rider's $7.00 claim is therefore not refundable at all.

The only line on which the rider can recover anything is the off-route ERP. The platform's closure-branch arithmetic recomputes the fare against the closure-adjusted optimal at $32.3460, and that recomputation already comprehends the $3.00 ECP Fort Rd eastbound line; POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding off-route ERP on top of the recomputed figure. The payable on that arithmetic is $2.70, which is the ceiling of the rider's recovery - nowhere near the $7.00 contested.

The contested gantry is a genuine crossing and not a phantom line. The nearest driver fix to the ECP Fort Rd eastbound gantry is 59.12 m, at fix index 96 on 2026-08-21 18:39:08, well inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 sets. There is accordingly no billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4) and no full refund of the fare on the rider's 'a gantry I would never have passed' theory.

Nothing in this record requires escalation. The trace is clean - 193 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s - so POL-RD-07's impairment limbs are not met and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; trip identifiers match across the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown, so POL-RD-10(2) is not engaged; and POL-RD-03 is invoked against an advisory that is present and within the trip window, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged either. The case is decidable on the merits and should be decided on them.

NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03, and on this rider-filed dispute it leaves the charged fare standing. payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0, so the state the driver seeks on everything except the statutory off-route ERP pass-through is the state that already obtains; the fee should not be reversed on the strength of a 24.6 km figure that the closure-adjusted optimal shows to be justified.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver. This ruling was made without human review; either party may appeal it once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The trip and the measurement. TRP-02839 was driven on 21 August 2026. The GPS trace EV-GPS-02839 measures 24.6 km against the booked optimal of 20.0 km on trip record EV-TRIP-02839, an excess of 4.6 km and 23% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates are passed (more than 0.8 km and more than 20%), so a deviation is established, and the trace figure governs over the rounded trip-record copy. The trace itself is sound: 193 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), and the escalation triggers in POL-RD-10(2), (3), (4), (5) and (8) are not engaged. The rider needed no extra corroboration under POL-RD-08 (deviation_claims_60d is 0), and the burden that shifted to the driver was discharged by a specific artifact and clause, not a general assertion.

The extra distance is excused. LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-02839-01 is on file and admissible at full weight: a HIGH-severity CLOSURE on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway towards ECP after Defu Flyover, active 17:53:08 to 19:20:08, which wholly covers the trip window of 18:23:08 to 18:55:08, with the platform recording that it intersects the route and overlaps the trip window, and a shortest lawful alternative of 23.0 km. The trace records zero fixes inside the closed segment's area, with a closest approach of 1,350.67 m - the closest test of POL-RD-03 limb (c) this record allows, and consistent with a route that leaves the corridor before the affected segment. The two submissions on limb (c) are answered together: the rider says it cannot be verified because the optimal route's own polyline is not in the record, the driver says the trace proves the diversion. On this record the advisory's own route-intersection fact plus the trace's avoidance of the closed area is the best evidence there is, and it supports exoneration. (If a party wishes to contest limb (c), the optimal route's polyline is the item that would settle it - that is the one open question in this case, and it does not need a referral.)

POL-RD-03's cap is 1.30 x (23.0 - 20.0) + 1.00 = 4.90 km, which exceeds the 4.6 km measured, so the whole excess is justified and the deviation is fully excused.

What follows. Because an exculpatory clause fully excuses the deviation, POL-RD-02 does not run at all - its own terms apply only where no exculpatory clause fully excuses the deviation. That disposes of both competing figures: the rider's $7.85 recomputation against the booked optimal route (35.01 - 27.16) and the driver's $2.70 recomputation against the closure-adjusted route (35.01 - 32.35) both fail, because no POL-RD-02 recomputation issues. The distance and time charges stand.

What is refunded. The one charge the rider recovers is the ERP line, ECP Fort Rd eastbound, $3.00 (EV-FARE-02839). It is off the optimal route (on_optimal_route false; optimal-route ERP $0.00). The crossing is genuine, not phantom: the nearest driver fix to the gantry is 59.12 m at 18:39:08, inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 sets, so the rider's 'a gantry I would never have passed' does not make out a billing-integrity failure, there is no POL-RD-09(4) referral, and no full refund follows on that theory. But the rider did not cause the closure either, so under POL-RD-09(2) that $3.00 is refunded as a standalone pass-through correction (the SGD 12.00 cap is not reached). Charged total $35.01; refund $3.00; the rider pays $32.01. The driver's submission that NO_ACTION would leave the present state standing is right as a description of POL-GEN-03, but the off-route ERP line is refundable, so the outcome is a partial refund of $3.00 rather than no action.

Referrals and compensation. No referral issues. POL-RD-06 does not fire: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 197 completed trips in 90 days (about 0.005), below both the 3-flag and the 0.05 tests, so there is no repeat-deviation pattern, no driver-conduct review, and no uplift - the deviation is not MATERIAL in any event (23% against 50%, 4.6 km against 8.0 km, and nil on the excess remaining after the POL-RD-03 adjustment). No driver compensation is due: the rider was billed the full 24.6 km the trace records, so there is no unbilled distance under POL-RD-04.

Profile fields. rating, lifetime counters and cancellation rates on either profile are context only under POL-GEN-01 and were not used to decide anything about this trip; the rider's mention of them was flagged by the referee and is correct as far as it goes.

Execution. The monetary effect is $3.00, below the SGD 8.00 automatic execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so it is released on issue.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
